subject: MedCentra DPIA template — gap analysis & evidence plan
messages:
From: Lisa Martin <lisa.martin@medcentra.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: privacy.team@medcentra.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPIA template for Redwood (MedCentra onboarding)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. As discussed, attached is MedCentra's standard DPIA template (v3) that we use for any vendor processing PHI or personal data. Our security team flagged a few sections that need explicit evidence: data flow diagrams, subprocessors list, retention & deletion commitments, and a short description of your encryption-in-transit and at-rest controls.

Can your team provide a completed template and an evidence pack by end of next week (21 Jan)? If you think that timeline is tight, tell us what you can deliver and when. Also note we prefer a single consolidated PDF for our procurement review, plus any supporting diagrams as separate files.

Attachments: MedCentra_DPIA_Template_v3.xlsx (Excel template)

Thanks,
Lisa Martin
Data Protection Officer | MedCentra Health
lisa.martin@medcentra.com
+1 (415) 555-0182


From: jordan.blake@redwood.com
To: lisa.martin@medcentra.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPIA template for Redwood (MedCentra onboarding)

Lisa — thanks for sending. We received the template and will scope the response. Plan below:

1) Quick gap analysis of the template and a prioritized evidence list (due Wed 14 Jan).
2) Draft completed DPIA + evidence pack (consolidated PDF + diagrams) by Tue 20 Jan.
3) Finalized deliverable for procurement by Thu 22 Jan (to allow for your review).

Marissa — I'll own the responses for processing & technical controls. Please start pulling the system architecture diagram and SOC 2 summary.
Lauren — please coordinate retention and DPA wording with Legal and flag any SCCs/DPA clauses we need to call out.

If MedCentra has specific HIPAA-related mapping expectations beyond the template, let us know now so we include it in the gap analysis.

I'll prepare the gap-analysis email for MedCentra first thing Monday.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jan 2026 08:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPIA template for Redwood (MedCentra onboarding) — initial evidence pull

Jordan / Lauren — I've started the evidence pull. Early notes and blockers below:

- System architecture: generating an updated PNG (redwood-system-architecture-jan2026.png). Will include network segmentation and where KV caches live relative to model hosting.
- SOC 2: attaching a short SOC2-Summary-Redwood.pdf (control summary + scope). Full report requires an NDA; procurement usually accepts the summary for first pass.
- Subprocessors: we have an exported list (SaaS infra providers + CDN). Need to confirm if MedCentra requires contract copies for each; procurement often asks for that later.
- Retention: default token retention is 30 days for hosted customers, but for Private/Dedicated customers retention is configurable — need Lauren to confirm the exact policy wording we can commit to for MedCentra.

Blocker: one question in their template asks for 'mapping to specific lawful bases for each processing activity' — we typically map at the feature/workload level rather than per-field. Do we want to produce per-field mapping for this enterprise customer?

I'll draft the gap analysis (short bullet list) and send to Lisa with the sample evidence attachments by EOD.

Attachments: redwood-system-architecture-jan2026.png, SOC2-Summary-Redwood.pdf

Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Program Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Lisa Martin <lisa.martin@medcentra.com>
To: marissa_coole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jan 2026 11:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPIA template for Redwood (MedCentra onboarding) — clarifications

Thanks Marissa — that looks helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Per-field lawful basis mapping is preferred for our DPIA reviewers given the mix of PHI and PII. If you can map the main fields (e.g., patient identifier, clinical notes, audio transcripts) to lawful bases and any special categories processing, that would speed approval.
- We need confirmation that Redwood supports encryption at rest using customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private deployments. If yes, please note which KMS integrations are supported (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP CMEK).
- Retention: for PHI we expect options to align with our retention schedules (default 30 days isn't sufficient). Please indicate maximum configurable retention and deletion SLA for dedicated environments.
- Subprocessors: a short list is fine now; we will request contracts for final procurement.

If you can provide the above as bullets and a consolidated PDF by end of Wed 14 Jan, we will run an internal pre-check and provide any follow-up questions.

Lisa

From: jordan.blake@redwood.com
To: lisa.martin@medcentra.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPIA template for Redwood (MedCentra onboarding) — response package delivered

Lisa — appreciate the quick clarifications. Attached is our consolidated response pack (Redwood_DPIA_Response_MedCentra_v1.pdf) which includes:

- Per-field mapping for core data elements (patient_id, clinical_notes, audio_transcripts, derived_embeddings) to lawful bases and categories.
- Statement on KMS support: we support customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private deployments (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP CMEK).
- Retention: default hosted retention is 30 days; Dedicated/Private deployments allow configurable retention up to customer-specified retention windows with deletion SLA of 7 days after retention expiry (we document deletion workflows).
- Subprocessors list (summary) and link to contracts view for procurement.
- System architecture diagram and SOC 2 summary included as separate attachments.

Attachments: Redwood_DPIA_Response_MedCentra_v1.pdf, redwood-system-architecture-jan2026.png, SOC2-Summary-Redwood.pdf

Next steps: if MedCentra wants language edits to the DPA/SCCs we can route to Legal and provide tracked changes; otherwise we can provide the procurement bundle and a signed summary via DocuSign (link below).
